operative_text.controlling:
3.8(1)  An originating application must
(a) be in Form 7,
(b) state the claim and the basis for it,
(c) state the remedy sought, and
(d) identify the affidavit or other evidence to be used in
support of the originating application.
(2)  If an affidavit is filed to support an originating application, the
affidavit must be confined to
(a) a statement of facts within the personal knowledge of the
person swearing the affidavit, and
(b) any other evidence that the person swearing the affidavit
could give at trial.

BOOK_A.commentary:
On when an Originating Application is appropriate, see R.3.2n.B.There are notices to the profession giving guidelines for email or digitally-filed documents, in the "News and Announcements"

part of the Court of King's Bench's website. See further R.13.14n.Rule 3.2n.B.4 contains long, detailed warnings about booking Originating Applications, and filing them (or anything else). There are now new potentially grave dangers, as there described. Ordinarily a party cannot get relief or go into issues, which are not in his originating pleading, and so an Originating Application seeking only declaratory relief (and costs) will not permit them.

And there are other discretionary grounds to refuse declaratory relief). On hearsay in affidavits and substance, see R.13.18n, and theCanmorecase. On double or treble hearsay, seeL.Y.v.R.Y. *5
An affidavit by a legal assistant is unacceptable except for noncontroversial matters, but it is done too often.Someone asserting prejudice should himself swear, not file an affidavit by his lawyer's assistant, who is at two removes.Especially if the prejudice asserted is unlikely in the context of the undisputed history of the suit. The dubious nature of news stories from the media, or items from the internet, as exhibits to affidavits, is stressed in theANC Timbercase. However,

sometimes a legal assistant has the most direct knowledge, e.g.of what communications did or did not occur.

BOOK_B.title: Originating applications and associated evidence
BOOK_B.operative_text_raw: (1) An originating application must (a) be in Form 7, (b) state the claim and the basis for it, (c) state the remedy sought, and (d) identify the affidavit or other evidence to be used in support of the originating application. (2) If an affidavit is filed to support an originating application, the affidavit must be confined to (a) a statement of facts within the personal knowledge of the person swearing the affidavit, and (b) any other evidence that the person swearing the affidavit could give at trial. 1. Test for amending originating application In Thomson v. Thomson, 2024 ABCA 293, the Court said: [28] The test for amending pleadings after they have closed is as follows: Assuming some modest amount of evidence is provided in support, any pleading may be amended, no matter how careless or late the party seeking the amendment, subject to four major exceptions: (a) The amendment would cause serious prejudice to the opposing party, not compensable in costs; (b) The amendment requested is hopeless; (c) Unless permitted by statute, the amendment seeks to add a new party or new cause of action after the expiry of a limitation period; or (d) There is an element of bad faith associated with the failure to plead the amendment in the first instance. [Emphasis added] Terrigno v Butzner, 2021 ABCA 18 at para 11, citing Attila Dogan Construction and Installation Co. v. AMEC Americas Ltd. 2014 ABCA 74 at para 25, additional reasons 2015 ABCA 9. The same test is applied where permission is required to amend an originating application: Aramark Remote Workplace Services Ltd v. Unite Here Local 47, 2023 ABKB 42 at paras 16, 17; Ingram v. Alberta (Chief Medical Officer of Health), 2021 ABQB 343 at paras 20-23, affirmed 2022 ABCA 97; Alberta March for Life Association v. Edmonton (City), 2020 ABQB 220 at para 14; McCargar v. Métis Nation of Alberta Association, 2017 ABQB 692 at paras 7–10, reversed in part 2018 ABCA 144.
